paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. God raised Joseph from the dungeon to the palace, and Pharaoh saw it for what it was. He said, "Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you." (Genesis 41:39) The wisdom wasn't Joseph's own. It came from God, and Joseph never took the credit.

Now look at what Joseph does with the new power. He doesn't throw a party for himself. He gets to work. He stores up the food before the hungry years come, and when the famine hits, "there was food throughout the land of Egypt." (Genesis 41:54) Preparing in the good years is what fed people in the bad ones. That's the whole lesson, and I'd say it's a good one for anybody with an oven.

Then there are the names of Joseph's two sons. Manasseh and Ephraim tell us Joseph saw God's hand in the hard years and in the good ones. He says, "God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction." (Genesis 41:52) So when you're in your own hard place, baker, keep your eyes on God, and keep your hands busy getting ready. God can bring good out of the hardest ground, and He can use you to feed others while He does it. And this story isn't over yet.
